definition: holding a layer on my hands and putting it back whenever it comes off

settled:
Dry skin costs me even when I am touching nothing, so the layer is maintained rather than reached for. Feeling dry is the failure, not the cue.

Every handwash strips it, and I put it back about five minutes later, once the skin is dry enough to hold it.

The five minutes is a squeeze between two limits. Sooner and the water is still there, so the lotion never forms a layer. Later and the unprotected minutes pile up cost. It is the tightest gap that still lets the lotion bind.

Bottles in more than a dozen places, all the same brand. Prompt only works if the bottle is wherever the handwash was.

One brand because the wrong texture or scent becomes a cost of its own instead of removing one. Found once, then the same everywhere.

There is no relief direction here. I never choose to go without the layer. Water takes it off, and putting it back is the only move.
